gaps.construct: v |= x[i] ^ y[i] (bitwise OR and XOR on bytes)
gaps.description: The doc lists only + - * / and mod; there are no bitwise operators. `bitwise_or` and `bitwise_xor` are invented word operators.

gaps.construct: constant-time execution with respect to secret contents (the function's entire reason to exist)
gaps.description: Information-flow labels cover where secret data may go, not whether control flow or timing depends on it. Nothing stops the compiler or a reader from replacing the loop with an early-exit comparison. Invented header `runs in constant time with respect to x and y`.

gaps.construct: byte type, byte arithmetic, and result int restricted to 0 or 1
gaps.description: The doc names Bytes but no single Byte type or byte literal; `0` is used as a byte. The 0/1 result fits a refinement (`Int with value 0 through 1`), which works well.

gaps.construct: returning a derived boolean from secret inputs
gaps.description: Unclear whether a comparison result derived from secret-labelled data must be declassified; a `declassifies` line is added to make the release explicit.

invented_syntax: runs in constant time with respect to x and y (header line)
notes: The arithmetic is trivial, but security-critical constant-time code needs a guarantee about timing that Scribe's information-flow labels do not cover; a checked 'secret-independent control flow' property would fit naturally next to `declassifies`. Bit operators are absent from the vocabulary entirely, which will block hashing, crypto, compression and wire-format code across the corpus.
